rv.q: The story of the impoverished Younger family whose recently deceased patriarch has left them with insurance money that may help realise their dreams, retains its power, with resonant themes of class, male chauvinism, assimilation and generational difference in the Black community.
A Raisin in the Sun by Lorraine Hansberry remains as impactful as it was when it premiered on Broadway 65 years ago.

cn.t: This revival of Hansberry's groundbreaking drama remains powerfully relevant, delivering a stirring examination of a Black family confronting segregation with a timeless message of hope that resonates as strongly today as it did 65 years ago.
